title: CORS: credentialed cross-origin read
summary: Prove a cross-origin page can read credentialed protected data. A reflected Access-Control-Allow-Origin header alone, without credentials and a real browser read, is not impact.
steps: On an observed endpoint returning test-owned sensitive data, send one untrusted canary Origin (not evil.com) and a no-Origin control.
SUBMIT signal: the response echoes the canary Origin in Access-Control-Allow-Origin AND sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Note Vary: Origin and whether the body is actually protected data.
Confirm with an OPTIONS preflight carrying Authorization and the real method, then a credentialed cross-origin read in execute_browser.
Keycloak: repeat on token, userinfo, and /auth/admin/realms/<realm>/users — header proof is enough; do not dump users. webOrigins should be explicit or '+', never '*'.

On PASS: the echoed-origin + credentials=true response with request evidence. queue_finding_followups(vuln_type='cors_credentials'); if proven on Keycloak, queue keycloak_password_grant and do not spray passwords.
KILL if headers suggest a misconfiguration but a real cross-origin browser read of protected data fails (credentials=false, or the data is public by design).
pass_signals: Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoes an untrusted Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
A cross-origin browser reads credentialed protected data
kill_signals: Headers suggest misconfiguration but browser access to protected data fails
credentials=false, or the response body is public by design
